content:
Title: Telecom Edge (Low-latency) POC — SOW & Pricing Draft
Owner: Ava Martinez (solutions-eng lead)
Status: In review — working draft for customer workshop (Dec 2024)

One-line summary:
Customer (Tier-1 telco) requests a 12-week proof-of-concept to validate a hybrid Redwood deployment: on-prem/to-edge nodes for sub-50ms RTT inference for real-time speech moderation and lightweight NLU. This doc outlines scope, phases, success criteria, resource assumptions, and an initial pricing model for services + capacity.

Background & goals:
- Business need: inline moderation & call routing decisions for live voice streams. Hard SLOs: per-token generation/embedding latency under 50ms tail for 1–4s audio windows; throughput scale for 250 concurrent channels in first phase.
- Why Redwood: unified runtime across Dedicated & Private with routing/fallback for capacity, KV caching for repeated prompts, and optimized kernels for trimmed seq lengths.
- Primary customer asks: low-latency edge inference, predictable unit economics, private network integration (MPLS+VLAN), SOC2-like auditability.

Scope (what we will deliver):
Phase 0 — Discovery (2 weeks)
  - Onsite workshop with customer's SRE, voice platform, and security (2 days) to gather latency profiles, network topology, and sample traffic.
  - Deliverables: discovery report, proposed deployment topology (edge pods + central fallback), and target perf metrics.

Phase 1 — Pilot (6 weeks)
  - Deploy 2 edge clusters (customer-managed HW or colocated at POPs) running Redwood Private runtime with 1 model family (quantized LLM for moderation + small NLU).
  - Integrations: RTP ingest adapter, light-weight pre/post-processing hooks, metrics + tracing to Redwood Console.
  - Deliverables: pilot deployment, runbook, perf / cost report, and a 1-week soak test.

Phase 2 — Production readiness & Handoff (4 weeks)
  - Hardening, HA config, autoscaling tuning, rollout policy (canary + auto-fallback to central model).
  - Handover docs, runbook, and 2 knowledge-transfer sessions for customer ops.

Success criteria (mutually agreed):
- 95th percentile inference latency < 60ms, 99th < 120ms for 1–4s audio windows in pilot environment.
- End-to-end moderation decision time (ingest -> decision) < 250ms for 90% of sampled calls.
- Throughput: support 250 concurrent channels during pilot with <5% error rate.
- Secure data path validated (TLS mTLS to Redwood control plane and optional KMS integration).

Assumptions (important):
- Customer provides edge compute (NVIDIA T4/GPU-equivalent) or we provide Dedicated reserved capacity (see pricing).
- Customer provides sample traffic and test harness (we will help instrument).
- Model selection limited to Redwood-curated families; additional model tuning or training out of scope.
- Network latency estimates provided during discovery will determine final topology.

Personnel & estimated effort:
- Solutions Eng: 2.0 FTE for pilot (6 weeks) — integration, deployment, tuning
- Platform Eng (private): 1.0 FTE for onboarding & HV config
- SRE (runbooks & handoff): 0.5 FTE during production readiness
- PM: 0.25 FTE overall (coordination)
- Total services days estimate: 40 engineering days (approx)

Initial pricing (draft) — two options depending on where customer hosts compute:
Option A — Customer-provided Edge HW (services only)
  - Discovery & architecture: $25,000 (fixed)
  - Pilot (integration & deployment): $80,000 (fixed, ~24 eng days)
  - Production readiness & handoff: $30,000 (fixed)
  - Optional 12-month support retainer: $8,000/mo (Silver) or $20,000/mo (Gold with 24/7 on-call + 1-hr escalation)
  - Travel & expenses: TBD (cap $10k)
  - Estimated total (project): $135,000 + optional support

Option B — Redwood-managed Dedicated edge (we provide reserved capacity + infra ops)
  - Discovery & architecture: $25,000 (fixed)
  - Pilot (deployment + infra ops): $110,000 (fixed, includes infra provisioning & 2-week soak ops)
  - Monthly reserved capacity (two edge clusters equivalent): $35,000/mo (includes baseline GPU reservation, monitoring, console access)
  - Private deployment license (one-time): $40,000
  - 12-month managed ops + SLAs: $45,000/mo (Gold) or $18,000/mo (Standard)
  - Estimated first-year cost (pilot + 3 months reserves + license + ops): ~$400k (ballpark; final sizing during discovery)

Price notes & rationale:
- Engineering day rates in fixed fees assume blended rate for senior+mid engineers; exact counts and day rates will be in final SOW.
- Reserved capacity pricing reflects lower per-token price but commitment required; optional autoscaling bursts billed separately.
- Security & compliance add-ons (KMS/HSM integration, enhanced audit logging) quoted separately.

Payment & contractual items:
- Standard 30% on signature, 40% at pilot completion, 30% at handoff for fixed-fee services.
- Reserved capacity billed monthly in arrears unless annual prepay agreed.
- Change requests outside SOW scoped via time & materials (T&M) estimate.

Operational constraints & risks:
- Customer network variability: packet loss/jitter can increase end-to-end latency; mitigation: colocate inference near RTP termination and use jitter buffers.
- Model mismatch risk: moderation model may require prompt engineering for telco use cases — allow 1 iteration for prompt tuning within pilot.
- Hardware procurement timelines: if customer buys hardware, lead time may push pilot start dates.

Workshop notes (summary from 2024-11-20 session):
- Customer emphasized multi-region POP coverage (APAC + EU + NA) in phase 2.
- Security: must support customer-managed keys (HSM) and detailed audit trails for decision provenance.
- Observability: want token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards (we showed Redwood Console mock).
- Integration: RTP -> transcriber (customer) -> Redwood inference -> policy engine -> enforcement. Several points to instrument for measurements.
- Open items captured: network diagrams, sample traffic capture, final model family selection, exact POP locations.

Open questions (to resolve in discovery):
- Will customer allow any outbound control-plane connectivity, or must control plane be air-gapped?
- Exact concurrency & peak burst profiles for voice channels (per POP).
- Which KMS provider (customer k8s KMS? cloud provider?) and audit retention window.
- Acceptance criteria thresholds for latency & decision correctness (customer must sign-off).

Next steps & action items:
- Redwood: produce final discovery checklist + pre-workshop packet (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2024-11-30)
- Customer: provide network topology + sample pcap and expected call concurrency (owner: telco eng lead, due: 2024-11-29)
- Schedule 2-day onsite workshop (target week of 2024-12-09)
- Redwood SE to prepare pilot runbook template and cost breakdown for HW vs Redwood-managed option (owner: Ava Martinez, due: 2024-12-06)

Appendix: quick sizing assumptions used for pricing
- 1 edge cluster = 8 x T4-equivalent GPUs (supports ~250 concurrent short-seq voice channels for our quantized model family)
- Central fallback cluster sized at 4 x V100-equivalents for overflow and model variant serving
- Pilot traffic estimate used: 250 concurrent, average request length equivalent to 60 tokens per call window

Notes: this is a draft for internal review and customer pre-read. Expect pricing & exact scope to shift post-discovery. Mark TODOs for legal (SLA language) and security (contractual MSA addendum).
